Streaming & Videos
You are welcome to stream and make videos of the game. No permission needed, and monetization is fine.

  • Please don't reveal key twists or trial verdicts in your titles or thumbnails, so your viewers get the surprise too.

  • Adding the game's name or a link to the Steam page in your description would be much appreciated.

  • Settings include a Streamer Mode that hides more sensitive images. Feel free to turn it on while streaming.

  • For collaborations or questions, find us on Discord:

Don’t Just Finish the Story. See Through Every Line.

In most visual novels, what a character says is all the player gets.

Are they lying?
What do they truly want?
Why have they suddenly started treating you kindly?
What is really hidden behind that seemingly harmless remark?

Usually, you have to wait for the story to reveal the answers.

But in The Bastard Who Rewrote the Empire, every line of dialogue can become a doorway.

You can accept the version a character gives you—or spend a limited ability use to uncover the other truths buried beneath their words.

Dialogue no longer has only one interpretation.

A single line can be read in five different ways.

One Line. Four Ways to Dig Deeper.

When someone tells you:

“Please believe me. I never wanted to hurt you.”

You can choose to do nothing and take their words at face value.

Or you can activate one of four different abilities.

Inner Voice

Peer directly into the thoughts they never say aloud.

They may apologize while secretly trembling with fear.
They may appear loyal while plotting how to use you.
They may act as though nothing is wrong while already falling apart inside.

What a character says and what they think may tell two entirely different stories.

Sincerity

Turn emotions and intentions into readable intelligence.

You can examine:

  • The Lie Value of a line;

  • The character’s current Affection toward you;

  • The true intention behind their words.

A tender promise may be ninety percent false.

A cold rejection may come from someone who simply refuses to put you in danger.

Numbers can expose the performance on the surface, but they may not fully explain why someone chose to lie.

Appraisal

Read a character’s identity, background, and hidden profile, or analyze an item’s value, composition, and purpose.

An unremarkable servant may possess a family background that should not exist.
An ordinary bottle of wine may contain an ingredient capable of changing the outcome of a trial.
A seemingly worthless object may become the key to turning the entire situation around.

Some lies are hidden in words.

Others are hidden in identities and objects.

X-Ray Vision

See through the clothes a character is currently wearing, or through the first layer obscuring whatever stands before you.

It can be a tool for uncovering secrets—or simply a way of satisfying a curiosity you should never have indulged.

You may discover something that was deliberately concealed.

Or perhaps, after gaining this power, you will simply begin crossing boundaries you never would have crossed before.

When you possess the power to peer at anyone, the real question is no longer what you can see.

It is:

When will you choose to stop?

You Cannot See Through Everyone

Your abilities are not unlimited.

Extra uses are bought in the Skills Shop with iron, an in-game currency you earn as you play (no real money involved)—so you must decide which person is worth investigating, which line deserves a closer look, and which secret might truly change the situation.

When the queen threatens you, will you check her Lie Value first—or read her mind?

When a companion promises to stay and protect you, will you trust her, or spend a precious ability use on her?

When someone tells an obvious lie, will you spend one of your limited chances to discover why they lied?

You cannot know every truth.

That means choosing what not to know is just as important.

The Same Scene Can Offer a Completely Different Reading Experience

On your first playthrough, you may spend every ability on your political enemies, trying to discover who is plotting against you.

On another playthrough, you can turn your attention toward your companions and uncover the fears, desires, guilt, and secrets they never voiced aloud.

Without the truth, a line may sound like a promise.
After seeing its Lie Value, it may become a test.
After reading the speaker’s thoughts, it may become a desperate plea for help.

Even when the scene remains the same, the information you possess, the way you understand each character, and your reasons for making a choice can be completely different.

The Bastard Who Rewrote the Empire does not simply ask you to replay the same story.

It lets you discover, on a second reading, another story that was there all along—one you never saw the first time.

After Death, You Become Hell’s Most Anticipated Star

An ordinary man from Hong Kong dies and is chosen by HELL TV, the broadcasting network of the underworld.

He is not sent to Heaven.

Nor is he cast straight into Hell.

He is sent to star in a TV show.

He awakens as Lucian, the kingdom’s bastard prince—only to find himself on trial for his life.

Someone has accused him of poisoning the crown prince.
The queen wants him silenced forever.
The Church is searching for a weakness it can exploit.
Every companion by his side hides a secret they cannot confess.

Beyond that world, the audience in Hell watches his every move through their screens.

He has only thirty days.

Within those thirty days, he must use the abilities granted to him by the underworld to see through lies, gather secrets, and build alliances—transforming himself from a bastard awaiting execution into someone capable of shaking the entire kingdom.

Because Hell has never wanted to watch a man live peacefully.

Hell wants a twist.

When the Human Heart Becomes a Number, Can You Still Trust Anyone?

Lies can be displayed as percentages.

Feelings can become Affection scores.

A person’s identity, value, and desires can all be analyzed through your abilities.

These powers allow Lucian to escape one death trap after another.

They also allow a man who could never control his own fate in life to experience, for the first time, the intoxicating feeling of having power over others.

At first, he only wants to survive.

Later, he begins to enjoy seeing through people.

When someone can know who is lying, who likes him, who is afraid—and even peer into everything another person refuses to reveal—

Is he using a system that can save him?

Or a power that is slowly becoming addictive?

The numbers you see may all be true.

But do those numbers represent the whole truth of a human being?

Key Features

A Five-in-One Dialogue Experience

Every line retains its original meaning while offering four additional interpretations through your abilities.

You Decide How Deeply to Read

Not every secret is revealed automatically. You must decide which character and which line of dialogue are worth investigating.

Four Abilities, Four Kinds of Truth

Read minds, judge lies and Affection, appraise characters and objects, and see through the first layer concealing what lies before you.

A Reading System Built Around Resource Management

Ability uses are limited. Every investigation is a choice about which information matters most.

A Visual Novel Designed to Be Replayed

Use your abilities on different characters to uncover entirely different stories hidden behind the same scenes.

HELL TV × Medieval Court-Intrigue Power Fantasy

Under the gaze of Hell’s audience, survive deadly trials, palace conspiracies, conflicts within the Church, betrayals, and assassination attempts.

Item Appraisal and Duplication

Discover the true purpose of different objects and use the Duplication Bag to create items capable of changing the course of events.

Truth Is Not the Same as Justice

When you can turn the human heart into data, you must also decide how you will use that power.

Will You Believe What They Say—or Look for Yourself at What Lies Beneath Their Words?

In The Bastard Who Rewrote the Empire, reading is not simply a way to receive a story.

Reading itself is your choice.

You are not only deciding what Lucian will say next.

You are also deciding:

How much truth are you willing to see?

You are Wilson a rookie baker who just opened a new bakery in west Berlin. Build up your dream business or spend all of your time at the bar! Explore the walled city, deliver people pastries and don’t forget customer isn’t always right!

Bake! or Make Coffee!

Youre running a bakery cafe at the end of the day. You have customers you need to satisfy even though some might be difficult.

Choose from tons of pastries!

Each have their own unique baking process. You can make anyhting you want in any order you want.

Navigate random events that take place in Berlin. Don't let your guard down.

This is Berlin after all, people are crazy here... Be careful.

YOUR FIRST VICTIM IS A BLADE OF GRASS


The Big Suck is an arcade incremental where you steer a tornado, earn cash from everything you wreck, and spend it on upgrades between runs.

At first, grass is a worthy opponent. A hay bale feels ambitious. A barn is personal.

Then the camera pulls back.

EVERY WRECK PAYS. SPEND IT ON A WORSE STORM


When the wind dies you get a damage report and a payday. Spend it in the upgrade tree: a wider pull, a longer clock, a nastier chain reaction.

Then touch down again and settle up with the barn that survived.

PICK YOUR CATASTROPHE


Past a certain size you stop being weather and start choosing what kind.

  • BECOME FIRE. Spread infernos from target to target.
  • BECOME THE FLOOD. Throw bow waves down whole streets, then run current through the wet ground.
  • BECOME WINTER. Hold still, let the cold spread, then crack one frozen block and take the district with it.
  • BECOME THE VOID. Open a hole and let matter stop pretending it is permanent.

Switch between touchdowns. Once a storm is yours, it stays yours.

THE WORLD FIGHTS BACK. IT GOES BADLY


Fire crews try to contain you. Bomb squads defuse your best chain reactions. Tanks roll in, jets scramble, and eventually somebody authorizes a weapon that should not be pointed at weather.

Catch the shells in your wind. Return them. Get paid for the inconvenience.

By then the map is not a place. It is the next thing you outgrow.

EARTH IS THE FIRST PLANET


Finish Earth's campaign and take your storm to ZORB, an alien world. Crack open its ore veins and spend CORES on permanent upgrades.

THE COWS GET A FARM


It seems only fair. TORNADO FARM is a cow-farm incremental inside the game. Grow your herd and earn permanent bonuses for your tornado.

WHAT'S IN THE GAME


  • About 5–6 hours to the main campaign finale. Start with grass. Finish by tearing the planet apart.
  • 66 achievements. About 12–18 hours to get them all.
  • 23 storm forms. 363 upgrades. Build your way from a light breeze to THE BIG SUCK.

THE BIG SUCK


A TORNADO WITH A BUSINESS PLAN.

THE BIBLE IS OUTLAWED. THE TRUTH IS BEING REWRITTEN.

Imagine Papers, Please, but instead of inspecting passports, you're deciding which Bible verses are authentic and which are dangerous lies.

In The Canon Keeper, the government has outlawed the Bible, destroyed nearly every copy, and replaced God's Word with corrupted Scripture. The last surviving underground churches are desperately fighting to preserve the truth.

You are a member of the resistance. Smuggled Scripture fragments arrive at your desk, and it's your responsibility to determine what is authentic, what has been altered, and what must be destroyed.

But be warned. Every mistake strengthens demonic forces threatening the last surviving underground churches.

INSPECT. DISCERN. DECIDE.

Every fragment is a test of your discernment.

Some passages are authentic Scripture. Others are completely fabricated. The most dangerous contain subtle changes, sometimes just a single word, designed to twist the meaning of God's Word.

Examine each fragment carefully. Search for inconsistencies, and determine whether the passage belongs in the Bible or the fire.

APPROVE the truth. REJECT the deception.

It sounds simple. Until the lies become almost indistinguishable from the truth.

EVERY MISTAKE GIVES DARKNESS MORE POWER

The Scripture you approve is copied and distributed to underground churches desperately trying to rebuild the Bible.

Approve corrupted Scripture, and false teachings spread as the Word of God.

Destroy authentic Scripture, and precious fragments of the truth are lost.

Every mistake weakens the resistance, strengthens demonic forces, and pushes the underground churches closer to destruction.

The resistance is barely surviving. They are counting on you to recognize the truth.

How many mistakes can they survive?

YOUR DESK IS YOUR BATTLEFIELD

You aren't fighting with guns or swords. You're fighting a war over the truth, one Scripture fragment at a time.

Use the tools available at your desk to:

  • Examine smuggled Scripture for errors and alterations.

  • Detect fabricated passages and subtle changes in wording.

  • Approve authentic Scripture for preservation or send corrupted fragments to the fire.

As the days progress, the pressure increases, and the deception becomes more difficult to recognize.

Sometimes the most convincing lie is only one word away from the truth.

BE STILL. PRAY. FIND THE TRUTH.

When the pressure becomes overwhelming, take a moment to pray.

Prayer slows time, giving you precious moments to examine the evidence and make your decision before time runs out.

But prayer doesn't remove your responsibility. You must still exercise discernment.

The truth is there. Will you recognize it?

You are not a soldier. You are not a prophet. You are an ordinary person entrusted with an extraordinary responsibility.

The government is determined to erase the Bible. The underground churches are on the brink of collapse. Demonic forces grow stronger with every failure.

And you are the one standing between the truth and its destruction.

Everything comes back to the final request of someone you loved.

KEEP THE WORD.

Will you preserve God's Word, or will your mistakes help destroy the last surviving churches?

GAME FEATURES

  • Papers, Please-style gameplay: Inspect, verify, approve, or reject smuggled Bible verses.

  • Biblical discernment: Identify authentic Scripture, altered passages, and completely fabricated verses.

  • Consequential decisions: Every mistake weakens the underground churches and strengthens demonic forces.

  • Prayer mechanic: Slow time through prayer when the pressure becomes overwhelming.

  • Increasing difficulty: Face more deceptive Scripture and greater pressure as the days progress.

  • Dark, story-driven setting: Experience a world where Christianity has been driven underground and God's Word is under attack.

  • A unique Christian gaming experience: Test your knowledge, observation, and discernment in a game unlike traditional Bible games.

THE WORLD IS LOSING THE WORD OF GOD. WILL YOU KEEP IT?

Play The Canon Keeper on Steam and begin your fight to preserve the truth.

Gameplay: A linear, story-driven 2D narrative adventure told through dialogue and character illustrations. Follow twelve-year-old Haechan's journey as he gets swept up in Korea's Donghak movement. Select scenes are brought to life through live-action footage filmed on location.

Background: Joseon, the 1890s. Twelve-year-old Haechan lost his mother to illness and his father to a tax he could never pay, and now works as a stable boy at a small relay station near Wonju — dreaming only of a way out.

One day he meets a fugitive old man wanted nationwide for a bounty of a thousand nyang. The old man turns out to be Choe Si-hyeong, the second leader of the Donghak movement.

Not knowing who he's really helping, Haechan starts carrying secret letters for the movement, and slowly begins to hear the old man's quiet teaching: Innaecheon, "people are heaven."

As the letters take him across Joseon and closer to the moment history already wrote for 1898, Haechan is pushed, again and again, to choose between his own survival and someone else's.

Note: This game is a work of fiction inspired by the historical figure Choe Si-hyeong and the Donghak movement. Certain characters, events, and details have been created or altered for storytelling purposes and do not accurately reflect historical fact.

The Cinder Throne is an Idler RPG where you fight enemies by waiting, customize your equipment and build to fit your playstyle and tackle harder and harder challenges.

Game Loop

Automatically fight enemies and loot them, explore various zones until you kill the final boss, upgrade yourself and try harder zones or difficulties (difficulties are personalizable), then repeat.

Loot

Enemies will drop loot that you can equip in 6-12 slots, each item will give different stats and they can be enchanted, enchanted items will give less stats but have spells attached to them.
Spells will synergize with your own stats and upgrades.

Upgrades

After a run, upgrade yourself in multiple Upgrade Trees, these trees will have various bonuses from small stat buffs to synergistic buffs, to powerfull buffs that add new mechanics to your character.
Some Paths will lock others, so you have to personalize your build and try to make synergies to be as powerfull as possible.

Conquer WorldsAfter conquering the Throne of Cinder nothing will stop you, conquer other worlds, keep only some of your upgrades and continue fighting in other worlds.
Conquering other worlds becomes more difficult the more worlds you've conquered.

The Clownhouse

Break into a cursed mansion.

Steal everything you can.

Escape before the Clown finds you.

Do it alone, or with up to 3 friends in online co-op.

The Clownhouse is a stealth horror extraction roguelite where every run is a gamble. Loot valuables, manage your sanity, and decide how long you're willing to stay before greed gets you killed.

The mansion changes every run. Layouts shift, dangers move, and the deeper you go, the worse things become. Most runs don't last long, but every escape makes the next one easier.

There are no weapons here. You survive by staying quiet, hiding in the dark, disguising yourself, improvising tools, and knowing when it's time to leave.

Survive Together — Co-op for Up to 4 Players

Break in alone, or bring up to three friends into the mansion with you.

  • Online co-op for up to 4 players. The mansion is hard enough alone — facing it together changes everything.

  • Split up to grab more loot faster, or stick close when the Clown starts hunting.

  • Coordinate distractions, barricade doors, and cover each other's escape.

  • More players means more loot to carry out — and more ways for a run to fall apart.

  • Prefer a lonelier nightmare? Every run can still be played solo.

Greed Keeps You Inside

Every run is a risk-reward gamble.

  • Search the mansion for cash, jewels, rare valuables, and hidden rooms.

  • Manage limited inventory space and weight. Every item you carry could mean leaving something better behind.

  • Escape with what you've found, or push deeper and risk losing everything.

  • Short, high-tension runs built for replayability.

The Mansion Wants You Gone

You're not alone inside.

  • The Clown stalks the halls relentlessly. Sometimes it kills. Sometimes it just watches and laughs while your sanity collapses.

  • The Butcher only hunts in the light. In darkness, he's harmless. Sometimes your flashlight is the most dangerous thing you own.

  • The Rabbit lurks through the mansion wearing a mask you'll desperately want for yourself.

Outsmart Them

You can't fight what hunts you. You survive by tricking it.

  • Wear disguises. Steal the Bunny Mask and walk among the mansion's horrors unnoticed.

  • Stay hidden. Turn off your flashlight, crouch through darkness, and avoid making noise.

  • Slow them down. Barricade doors, deploy distractions, and use crafted tools to buy yourself precious seconds when escape is the only option.

  • Move quietly. Find gear that muffles your footsteps and keeps attention away from you.

Hold Onto Your Mind

The longer you stay, the harder it becomes to think clearly.

  • Sanity constantly drains inside the mansion, especially when the Clown decides to toy with you.

  • Craft cocktails from looted alcohol to steady your nerves and survive longer runs.

  • Solve puzzles and unlock sealed rooms hiding the mansion's most valuable rewards.

Key Features

  • Play solo or in online co-op for up to 4 players.

  • Stealth horror extraction gameplay.

  • Fast, replayable roguelite runs.

  • Procedurally generated mansion layouts.

  • Risk-reward looting and extraction loop.

  • No combat. Only stealth, hiding, and survival.

  • Build barricades, deploy distractions, and improvise survival tools.

  • Unique enemies with different behaviors and weaknesses.

  • Disguise system that lets you blend in with the mansion's horrors.

  • Sanity system affected by darkness and enemy encounters.

  • Inventory management with limited space and weight.

  • Hidden rooms, puzzles, and rare valuables.

  • Persistent roguelite progression between runs.

Early Access

The Clownhouse is in active development, and now playable in solo and online co-op for up to 4 players. Early Access lets you experience the core extraction-horror loop now while new enemies, mechanics, areas, progression systems, and content continue to be added and refined over time.

The Clues is a challenging logic deduction game set in a charming town of animals.

Step into the paws of a cat detective and investigate mysterious cases across Paw Town. Read the clues, connect the information, and determine who is Criminal and who is Innocent to recover the town’s missing items.

Pure Logic. No Guessing.

Every conclusion can be logically proven from the clues available to you.

Compare clues, eliminate possibilities, and follow the chain of deductions until only one answer remains.

No guessing. No luck. Just logic.

Handcrafted & Uniquely Solvable

Every puzzle and every clue is handcrafted by the developer.

A dedicated validation system ensures that each puzzle is logically consistent and has a unique solution. The system only verifies the puzzles — it never generates them.

How Far Can You Go?

The puzzles start simple, but they won’t stay that way.

Each chapter brings tougher clues and deeper deductions, putting your logic skills to the test.

How far can you make it?

The Crown is a visual novel set in the early 2000s urban East Coast, where you guide a character from age 12 through age 18, on the road to becoming an underworld boss.

As you play, your character will grow and change.  You'll meet people who may offer you work or threaten you.  Challenges will become harder and you'll succeed or fail based on your preparation and a little luck.

When the game ends, your score will be applied to grant Profile Points that accumulate across runs.  The interesting things you do will also unlock new starting Experiences, Contacts and Equipment.  This means your next character can be stronger and explore differently.

Each ending will be determined by your choices and strategy.  You may die, go to prison, or simply give up on crime as a career. Or you may take the first steps on the path to being a boss in your chosen profession.

ABOUT THE GAME

The Emperor has placed a bounty on an artifact called the Crown of the Vermillion Devil — enough gold to retire a king. Adventurers from every corner of the known world are chasing it. Your trail has led you here: a rain-soaked fishing village on an isolated island at the edge of the map, where the lampposts barely hold back the dark, the locals are going strange, and something older than memory is watching from the shadows.

Crown of the Vermillion Devil is a narrative text adventure RPG. Choose your class, build your character, and navigate a world built on branching dialogue, hidden stat checks, and decisions that carry real weight. Every conversation is an opportunity — or a trap waiting to happen.

A WORLD COMING APART

Something is wrong with the island. The wrong kind of wrong — not bandits or bad weather, but something that gets into the cracks between things. Townsfolk acting strange. A refined gentleman who stands in the rain without getting wet. An old woman who screams warnings that don't quite make sense, then vanishes without leaving footprints.

The further you venture from the docks, the worse it gets. An ancient order of knights reduced to a single young man filing reports no one reads. A lizardman tribe collapsing from within, its Elder dying, its new chieftain something that is not quite what it appears to be. A village where everyone wakes up every morning covered in blood they don't remember. 

A god whose name no one has spoken in ten thousand years, stirring at the bottom of everything like sediment disturbed by a passing boot.

Crown of the Vermillion Devil draws heavily on Lovecraftian themes of cosmic dread, forgotten divinity, and the particular horror of realizing that the thing hunting you is not hunting you at all — you are exactly where it wants you to be.

FEATURES

Three playable classes — Fighter, Rogue, and Magic User — each with distinct capabilities, stat spreads, and starting equipment that shape how the world responds to you

A deep branching dialogue system with hidden stat checks across Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Charisma, and more — different builds unlock different paths, outcomes, and story revelations that other playthroughs will never see

Turn-based combat with spells, consumable items, status effects, and a meaningful ally system — the companions you recruit fight alongside you, and how many of them are standing at the end depends on choices made long before any battle starts

A cast of original characters with their own histories, agendas, and arcs — a Red Lions soldier who writes incident reports no one answers, a dryad whose tree has been burned, a shrine maiden who woke up on a stone table with no memory of falling asleep.

A world map navigated on foot, with every region carrying its own atmosphere, hazards, and things that do not behave correctly.

Dungeons and interiors that reward observation — locks that yield to patience or strength, traps that punish carelessness, rooms that remember whether you have been in them before.

An original score that shifts with your location — from the rain-soaked docks of Plaeti to the silence of an emptied city to the particular quiet of somewhere ancient that has been waiting.

Multiple endings with meaningfully different outcomes, shaped by everything you have done across the full length of the campaign.

THE WORLD

The island is larger than it first appears, and most of it does not want you there.

From the docks of Plaeti to the lizardman swamps of the south, the forest roads of the interior, the ruins of a city no one fled from, a tomb built for a king and repurposed by people who do not know what they are disturbing — Crown of the Vermillion Devil is a game about following a thread through a world that is actively unraveling. The Crown is real. The bounty is real. What you find at the end of the trail is something else entirely.

Two divine forces have been at work on this island for longer than anyone alive can remember. One of them wants to be found. The other has almost entirely forgotten its own divinity. The artifacts they left behind still work. Whether that is good news depends on what you do with them.

A NOTE ON TONE

This is not a game about chosen heroes. It is a game about someone unraveling a mystery into somewhere they should probably not have gone, and having to decide — incrementally, at each fork — what kind of person they are willing to be about it. The writing aims for the literary end of the genre: dry, precise, occasionally funny in the way that very bleak things are sometimes funny, and genuinely interested in its characters as people rather than obstacles.

If you have ever wanted a text RPG that trusts you to read carefully and rewards you for doing so, this is that game.

Add us to your Wishlist to follow development as we work toward release. Your support makes the difference.

The Cup is a free 1v1 creature card battler and roguelike deckbuilder, broadcast live: real animals and cryptids, and dice printed on every card that rolls. You coach a survivor and a line of three creatures. Every turn you play one card and make one attack, then the die TV decides how hard it lands while BroadcASH and BOBcast call it from the booth. Knock out all three of theirs and the match is yours.

THE DIE DECIDES. YOU CHOSE THE DIE.

Every creature is printed Safe, Swingy or Jackpot. Safe hits for the number on the card. Swingy rolls. Jackpot can miss outright, and a natural can wipe a creature off the board. You pick the risk when you draft, and everybody watches it land. There is no skip button, because the animations are the interface.

EVERY CARD DOES EXACTLY WHAT IT SAYS

Any of your creatures can hit any of theirs. No lanes and no hidden rules: the card is the rule, and the feed spells out every hit, reflect and knockout as it happens. A dome that hands damage straight back. A bee that stings once and goes to the Pit for it. Three a side, and three to six minutes a match once you know the rules.

TONIGHT'S FIGHT CARD

  • 59 contestants and 9 survivors from the United States, Canada and Mexico, every one a real animal or a cryptid, each with a checkable file

  • THE ROAD: ten cases against invasive species in one run, with HALFTIME in the middle. Draft creatures and kits as you go, and a knockout is gone for the road

  • Matches against the House, dealt or drafted, as many as you want

  • Live 1v1 on Steam from the full release on December 3

  • Every match written to tape, with highlights and replays

  • A shelf of mugs to earn, and a score composed in-house

THE STATE OF THE BROADCAST

Every painting on a card is commissioned from a human artist and credited on the card, one creature at a time, and the creatures still waiting wear placeholder art. The invaders are real photographs. The survivors' kits are drawn from public-domain history, with each source one click away.

The demo is out now: THE ROAD, the tutorial and matches against the House, offline. Card art by @chioart08, @prayogaardip, Ondřej Tichý, @tmcglynnart and Awesam.

The game's text and voices are in English. A broadcast of the Galactic Athletics Commission.

THE WORLD FORGOT PSARA. PSARA REMEMBERED YOU.

Psara is still there, beyond a black sea, on an island no map or mind can hold for long. When Elias Whitmore begins dreaming of a dead lighthouse and shores that speak in his own voice, he follows the route leading to the island. But its abandoned streets do not merely feel empty. They feel as though they have been waiting for him.

The Dark Forest Calls is a story-driven first-person survival horror game that binds light, sound, and memory into a single threat system. Explore fog-shrouded Psara, reconfigure its failing power network, manage scarce resources, and piece together why the island slipped out of the world's memory.

LIGHT IS NOT SAFETY

Darkness conceals your movement, but it also steals your sight. Restoring a generator can bring doors and machinery back to life and open new routes. Yet every running engine, open flame, and violent sound sends a pulse through the unseen network beneath the island.

Power is both access and invitation. Know when you need the light, and when you need to extinguish it.

SILENCE IS A RESOURCE

The creatures roaming Psara react to light and sound. Running, firing a weapon, knocking something over, or activating a machine at the wrong moment can reveal your position. Read the space, identify your exits, and manage silence as carefully as ammunition.

CHOOSE YOUR FIGHTS

Melee weapons and firearms are powerful, but every confrontation has a cost. Ammunition and healing supplies are limited. Choose your target, control the distance, time each attack, and remember that survival sometimes means leaving a fight unfinished.

NOTHING HERE REMEMBERS THE SAME THING

Psara's zombies are not the result of an ordinary outbreak. Their names and identities are gone, leaving old duties, fears, hunger, and fragments of ritual to reshape what remains.

Some carry light. Some guard a door or machine without end. Others awaken bodies that should have remained still. Before committing to a fight, learn what the creature in front of you is still trying to repeat.

READ THE ISLAND PIECE BY PIECE

Search the harbor, fog-bound settlements, power facilities, mountain passages, and underground tunnels. Conflicting journals, maintenance reports, clinical records, and voice recordings recount Psara's final days from different points of view.

No document tells the whole truth. Neither does Elias.

YOU ONLY HAVE WHAT YOU CAN CARRY

Divide limited inventory space between weapons, ammunition, fuel, medical supplies, keys, and objects that matter to the story. Use the power network and the tools you discover to reach sealed areas. Decide what to leave behind without knowing what the next path will demand.

ANSWER THE CALL

The evidence you uncover, the accounts you trust, and the memories you choose to preserve will change the meaning of your final decision.

Psara was forgotten for a reason. Some places should remain forgotten. Some mistakes refuse to be.

Ghost Archive is a meta-horror interactive archive game. You are an investigator granted access to the "Paranormal Event Archive Management System." Browse classified case files, search for keywords, piece together clues — and uncover the truth behind a series of unexplained disappearances spanning over a century.

But as your investigation deepens, you begin to realize: the archives aren't just being read. They're reading you.

Key Features:

  • 🔍 Archive Exploration: 29+ unique case files — manuscripts, reports, diaries, autopsy records, and more

  • 📝 Keyword Search System: Type the right keywords to unlock new files, simulating real investigative work

  • 👁️ Resonance & Control Dual Tracker: Every choice you make is recorded. Every path you take leaves a trace

  • 🌐 Whisper Network: Eerie messages left behind by other "investigators"

  • 🏆 Multiple Endings: Your level of control determines your fate — Tracker, Witness, or Symbiote?

The Long Night fell once, and it is coming back.
While one forge still burns, it cannot close over the world.
You are not a king. You are not a hero.
You are the smith who keeps the ember lit.

One rule, and it changes everything


Nothing happens while you are away.

Not the forge queue. Not the village. Not the countdown to the next warband. Close the game and the world holds its breath; open it again and it exhales exactly where you left it — same iron on the anvil, same seconds left on the wave clock.

This is a deliberate design decision, not a missing feature. There is no harvest waiting for you when you come back, so there is no reason to come back out of guilt. The session is the game. If you are looking for a number that grows in your pocket while you sleep, this is the wrong forge.

Prosperity and danger are the same coin


Buy iron, wood, leather and coal. Hammer them into daggers, swords, armour, bows and shields. Sell them to the adventurers who walk into your shop, and put the gold back into a faster forge, a longer queue, a village that feeds itself.

Then they come for the light. Every weapon you hammer out is a spark thrown at the dark — and the brighter your forge burns, the more of them see it. That is not flavour text bolted onto an economy. It is the economy.

What grows around the anvil


A village. Houses fill with people who arrive on their own schedule. Give them a trade — woodcutter, tanner, collier, farmer, instructor — and they feed the forge with raw material instead of just eating your grain. Eleven jobs, eleven buildings, and morale that sours if you let them go hungry.

A wall. The warbands are not random encounters. Every bandit is someone who found a splinter of dark steel and could not put it down, and the metal whispers the same order to all of them: go to the forge in the valley and put it out. You recruit from your own population, equip them with what you made yourself, arrange them in formation, and fight a turn-based battle you can actually direct.

A road out. Ten expeditions, each with a named boss and a weakness that means something: the axe splits the man who was once a woodcutter, the hammer dents the plate another one stole. Six destinations are the human kingdom of bandits. The last four are what was standing behind it.

A myth you assemble yourself. Nobody narrates it at you. It is scattered across item descriptions, boss epitaphs and material lore, and the Codex fills in as you earn the fragments. Play the whole game without reading a line and it works fine. Read them, and the ordinary metal you have been farming since your first wave starts to look very different.

Three tempers


  • Normal — Fallen units retire wounded and come back whole. The calm temper.
  • Hard — Tougher enemies, an extra minion per fight, and the fallen need treatment before they can fight again.
  • Permadeath — The fallen are gone, and their equipment comes back to your anvil bent. Reaching the final boss at all is roughly a coin flip. It is meant to be brutal.

The forge in numbers


  • 14 recipes on the anvil, from a bare dagger to the Dawn Sword
  • 11 village jobs and 11 buildings
  • 31 milestones, each with a reward
  • 10 expedition destinations, every one with a named boss
  • Fully localised in English and Spanish
  • Zero emoji — every icon is bespoke art

Autosaves every 30 seconds and on exit, with atomic writes and a backup that survives a corrupt save.

The Day I Became a Werewolf

The Day I Became a Werewolf is a first-person narrative game with horror and sci-fi elements. You play as an unlucky scientist living in a run-down house whose latest research has gone horribly wrong. Every day is a race against time to find a cure before your condition destroys everything.

Research

Your computer is your most valuable tool. Read scientific papers, browse emails, analyze research, and uncover hidden clues. Every discovery brings you one step closer...

Shop

Order equipment and supplies that may help you. Spend your money wisely. Every purchase could bring you closer to a cure... or become a desperate last resort.

Find a Cure

Make progress every day. Time is running out, and every full moon brings new dangers.

Don't Get Caught

The police are investigating a series of mysterious attacks, and you're running out of excuses.

The Derailed: Devour the Harvest - a first-person psychological horror game in the walking simulator genre.

Average playtime: 60 minutes

Unlike the others, you refused to accept the loss. Now you will have to pay for it.

Within the walls of a half-forgotten factory, reason will no longer help you - only by abandoning it can you make it to the end.

Game Features:

  • Walking simulator gameplay;

  • Interact with objects and solve puzzles to progress;

  • Uncover the mystery hidden beneath the crumbling factory;

  • Immerse yourself in a haunting environment with detailed locations;

  • Immersive 3D audio that pulls you in completely;

  • A short experience designed to be completed in one sitting, keeping the tension until the very end.

email: deformeddreams@gmail.com

The Endless Harvest: Idle Farm Defender

There is good soil here. A river that turns the wheels, hills that hold the evening light, and a village that has learned to sleep with one eye on the southern road.

The Endless Harvest is an idle village-builder crossed with a tower defense. You claim land, put up farms, mills and animal pens, and spend what they produce on towers, upgrades and research. Waves of raiders arrive on a timer and get stronger every time. Your goal is to grow the economy fast enough to out-build them and push as deep into the wave count as you can. Production keeps running while the game is closed, so you make progress even when you're not playing.

Build a Village That Pays for Itself

Claim the valley one plot at a time. Cottages, mills, coops, fields, water wheels turning with the current of the river. Every building produces. Every prop you scatter down a lane adds another percent on top. Close the game and the coffers keep filling — come back tomorrow to a fruitful harvest waiting at the gate.

Thirteen Towers, Thirteen Answers

No two towers work the same way. Each one has a mechanic of its own and a perk that unlocks as the waves climb, and each one takes its own orders — hit the closest, the furthest, the toughest, the weakest. The Blacksmith sharpens whole tower types at once, paid for in Energy your own windmills and water wheels generate.

A Harvest Worth Defending

Crops that grow on a real clock and scale further the deeper you get. Five kinds of livestock. Farmhands, animal handlers and turbine crews who live in your cottages and keep working long after you've logged off.

Research That Runs Overnight

The Laboratory costs gold, food, energy — and real hours. Run up to four benches at once. Nothing here is capped, nothing expires, and none of it stops when you close the window.

When the Line Breaks

Summon Vespera at the Altar: an archer hero, and the one soldier you command yourself. Four spells on standby for the moment a wave gets through. Ten boosts you can buy again and again. A Marketplace that quietly pays you interest on the gold you never got round to spending.

Nowhere to Stop

No wave gates. Nothing sealed behind a chapter you haven't reached. Just a curve that runs out somewhere past wave 11,000, and a village that grows to meet it — for as long as you want to keep growing.

You’ve been called to inspect a mysterious museum. Its owner claims that a strange aura surrounds some of the exhibits. Restore the works of art, uncover the truth behind the presence lurking within its halls, and discover whether some secrets were meant to remain hidden.

But something is watching you.

The further you progress, the more the museum seems to change around you… And the more this presence reacts to your actions.

🎨 Restore what was corrupted

Explore the museum and find the missing fragments of mysterious statues and paintings. Restore the corrupted works to cleanse them of the corruption surrounding them and unlock new galleries.

👁️ Something is watching

The museum is never truly silent. As you progress, a presence begins to react to your actions. The more you restore, the more determined it seems to become to stop you.

🏛️ Explore a living museum

Discover galleries filled with statues, paintings and forgotten relics. As you restore the museum, the world around you begins to change. Observe your surroundings, uncover clues, and piece together the story hidden within these walls.

The deeper you venture, the more the museum seems to respond to your presence. There are no weapons to rely on. Instead, you must observe, investigate, and understand what is happening around you.

Restore what was corrupted. Discover what should have stayed hidden.

Will you uncover the truth... or set it free?

You wanted followers. You wanted fame. You wanted that one perfect moment where the numbers just keep climbing and the world can't look away. Step up. Press Start. I'll give you everything you ever wanted. All it costs is one more spin.

THE FINAL LIKE is an authentic UK fruit machine twisted into a social-media nightmare. Holds, nudges, gambles, feature entries, cash ladders and jackpots work like the real thing - but every mechanic has been reimagined around the creator grind. Build your following. Chase sponsors. Dodge Copystrikes. Go viral.

And try not to notice when the machine starts changing the rules.

At the centre of it all is the Adaptive Construct Engine - ACE. It watches how you play, reacts to your wins and losses, and has very definite opinions about who deserves to walk away with its money.

Beneath the horror is a fully realised UK Fruit machine - also known as an AWP (Amusement With Prizes), with more than 80 individually controlled feature-board lamps, cash ladder, progressive jackpot, five bonus game types, fully featured LIVESTREAM bonus game, genuine holds, nudges and gambles, and all the wonderfully questionable machinery of the British fruit-machine experience.

And for those who know: the entire thing runs on proper compensator systems, modelled on the real machines.

Play the full experience in a dark arcade with ACE watching every move, or switch to Pub Mode for a warmer, traditional fruit-machine experience without the existential dread.

ACE sees everything. ACE remembers everything. And ACE DOESN'T like losing.

The dead still lie. Sorting that out is your job now.

On the tenth floor of the afterlife’s Chancellery, another soul approaches your desk. Their paperwork is in order. Their story is ready. All they need is your stamp - if you believe them.

The Final Stamp is a first-person detective game about investigating the lives of the dead and deciding where they belong: Hell, Heaven, or Purgatory. You have their belongings, their testimony, a few questionable instruments, and a rulebook with an entry for every sin.

Hear their side

A truck driver talks about the crash and his family. Johny Goldstein talks about his charity work. Everyone arrives with a story. Getting the rest of it takes some work.

Ask questions, catch contradictions, and return with evidence. Confront a soul with what you’ve found and listen as their explanation changes. Sometimes the new version sounds even more convincing.

Some answers require a call to Hell

Hold the Candle near a soul and watch its flame change colour to reveal a sin. Examine belongings through the Lens, test a suspicion with the Camera, or tune the Radio to a conversation from the past.

Need a record checked? Pick up the phone. The afterlife has departments, extensions, and employees who need you to explain exactly what you’re asking for.

Build your case, word by word

Words from documents and testimony become tiles on your desk. Combine them with other clues to reconstruct events, establish a motive, and build the grounds for your judgment.

How someone died is just the beginning. What they did before that tends to raise more questions.

One stamp. Three eternities.

Consult the Codex, choose a destination, and fill out the routing form. Nine circles of Hell, seven levels of Heaven, seven stages of Purgatory. Somewhere in there is a place for the person sitting across from you.

A convenient explanation could send a murderer to Heaven. A suspicious detail could mean nothing at all. Decide whether you know enough, then stamp the form and send it into the urn.

Your own case is still open

The Chancellery holds traces of the clerks who worked here before you. Explore the office between cases and find out how you ended up on this side of the desk.

Some souls hide a different truth on another playthrough, so recognising a face won’t give you the answer. Your own story leads to one of two endings, shaped by how you do your job.

Wishlist The Final Stamp. The Chancellery is hiring.

Free demo. It covers your first ten weeks as a footballer and match fixer, and the career you start carries into the full game on the same save, with no restart.

Everyone has a price. What's yours?

Football made you famous. The syndicate made you rich. THE FIXER is a narrative career sim where you live both lives at once: the rising star chasing titles on Saturday, and the fixer selling pieces of the match all week long.

ONE WEEK IN THE LIFE OF A FIXER

  • Monday, wake-up. Headlines, rumours, the fallout of what you did.
  • Tuesday, network. Lifestyle, family, contacts: grow the web that protects you.
  • Wednesday, fixing. The syndicate's offers arrive: a provoked yellow card, a missed sitter, a thrown match for a fortune.
  • Thursday, cover-up. Bets and sabotage on one side; laundering fronts and damage control on the other.
  • Friday, prep. Sharpen your legs, or your alibi.
  • Saturday, match. Play it live, minute by minute, or take the express result. Same consequences either way.
  • Sunday, debrief. The week's bill arrives. All of it.

MATCHES YOU CAN BEND

Live text matches with real stakes: tactical calls with visible success odds, fixes to pull off in the moment, a live betting window priced by an honest bookmaker, and momentum that swings with every duel. Pay the referee and the whistle goes quiet: a penalty, a red card for the opposition, and total impunity on the pitch. But the cameras see what the referee will not.

THE WORLD CLOSES IN

Your suspicion climbs with every dirty trick, and if it reaches 100, the run ends. The higher it goes, the more every press conference turns into a trap: the reporter slips in loaded questions, and you no longer get to duck them, you answer. Behind the scenes, a journalist opens an investigation that ripens week after week, right up to a finished dossier. One of them makes it personal: their byline is on every damning story, they come back season after season, and they never forget. Nothing stays buried for long. A case you thought was closed reopens, the referee you had in your pocket turns on you, and a trial can bring the whole thing down. And every dirty euro you pile up without laundering keeps the pressure rising, until the day the taxman asks where it came from.

A REAL FOOTBALL CAREER, TOO

Titles, the captain's armband, transfers, awards ceremonies, and a Cup of Nations every four seasons. Dialogue choices resolve with visible dice rolls. You can try to play it clean. The game will tempt you anyway.

BUILD YOUR LEGEND ACROSS LIVES

13 retirement verdicts, 8 ways to lose everything, a Hall of Careers that archives every life, and a legacy system: each finished career unlocks starting perks, backgrounds and mandates for the next one. The world remembers who you were.

Build a legend, or burn it all down.

The Fly’s Fantastic Adventure is a 2D run-and-gun platformer where you play as an innocent little fly who finds an unusual weapon: a fruit fly that shoots for him.

Run, jump, shoot, and fight your way through colorful worlds filled with strange enemies, tricky platforming, chaotic bosses, and plenty of insect-sized danger. What starts as a small adventure quickly turns into a battle for survival, as the spider that has always been chasing you becomes your greatest threat.

Use different weapons, explore varied levels, defeat bizarre bosses, and help the fly stand up against the spider once and for all.

Features:

  • Fast 2D run-and-gun platforming

  • Multiple weapons, including spread shots and web shots

  • Unique worlds filled with strange insect enemies

  • Chaotic boss battles against bizarre creatures

  • Optional minigames and secrets to discover

  • Single-player arcade action with a cartoony style

A tiny fly may not seem like much, but with the right weapon and enough courage, even the smallest hero can fight back.

STORY

Writer Wang Ran has been having a run of bad luck lately.

His wallet is gone, his new book is making no progress, and an inexplicable restlessness keeps gnawing at him.

What he cannot let go of even more is the girl named Hu Li — since the last time they parted, she has vanished without a trace.

Following the few clues he has, Wang Ran heads deep into the mountains.

A village shrouded in thick fog all year round appears before him.

The people here worship the Immortals of their own families —

the Fox Immortal, the White Immortal, the Willow Immortal... and a higher deity known as Mist Granny.

Here, an ancient rite known as the Rite of Sui-Banishing is being held.

Wang Ran had only wanted to find Hu Li and leave.

But once he becomes the Avatar of the White Immortal, there is no turning back.

When night falls, the being known as Sui begins to kill.

By day, the relationships torn apart by suspicion prove even deadlier than the night.

And Hu Li, whose whereabouts can never be found, seems bound to it all by countless hidden threads.

The fog grows thicker and thicker.

Who will still be alive when the rite comes to an end?

CHARACTER

Wang Ran (Protagonist)

A struggling novelist.

Because he lost his wallet, his journey starts badly — and he soon realizes that this was merely the beginning of his troubles.

Swept up in the village's rite, he must choose again and again between protecting others and saving himself.

Demon Rose

An uninvited witch.

From a distant city, she reads Wang Ran's manuscript through some special means.

Harsh yet precise, she is the sternest reader — and perhaps the most clear-sighted onlooker.

Bai Yu

Daughter of the Bai family.

Hot-tempered and sharp-tongued, she never gives anyone a pleasant face — yet she is the one who reveals the village's deepest secrets to Wang Ran.

Behind the half of her face she keeps hidden lies a failed past.

Hui Xiaoman

Daughter of the Hui family.

She always keeps her head down and stumbles over her words, as if afraid of everyone.

But at the rite's most critical moment, you will see a completely different side of her.

Qing Yi

The Shrine Maiden presiding over this rite.

Dignified in manner and measured in speech, she never lets a single superfluous emotion slip.

Every decision she makes seems carefully calculated — the question is, what is she really calculating?

Gu Shanzi

A young man of the village who tends to everyone's daily needs.

Taciturn and never one to defend himself — even when everyone suspects him of being Sui.

FEATURES

· A mystery folk-horror visual novel set in a secluded mountain village

· A murder mystery revolving around the rite — someone dies every night. Who is Sui?

· A main story woven from multiple intertwining character routes

· Exquisite CGs and character art paired with immersive sound design

· A tale of trust and betrayal, protection and sacrifice, and the line between fiction and reality

Catch Insects

Catch a variety of quirky insects as they crawl, buzz, and scuttle across each biome. Discover new species and fill your collection as you explore further.

Brew Potions

Turn your insect haul into magical potions and brew up powerful concoctions for more magical essence.

Upgrade Abilities

Grow stronger with upgrades that make catching insects faster, easier, and more rewarding. Improve your tongue’s range, speed, damage, and more to build the perfect frog.

Discover New Biomes

Venture and discover new environments filled with unique insects and surprises. Each biome brings new creatures to catch and new opportunities to grow.

Features

  • Live Out Your Frog Fantasies
    Stretch out your tongue and catch insects like a real frog. The longer your tongue, the more bugs you can grab!

  • Collect All Kinds of Insects
    Discover a growing variety of insects as you explore different environments. Catch them all and see what you can find.

  • A Fairy Tale With a Twist

    Inspired by the classic Frog Prince fairy tale, but with a twist. Expect plenty of parody, silly situations, and a prince who has to work to restore his human form.

    Relax, catch bugs, watch numbers go up, and steadily work your way toward becoming a frog prince once again.

You play a goblin in the service of the Demon King. A new party of heroes sets out for your lair every morning, and each night you prepare for their arrival.

There is no time limit at night. Sneak into the heroes' camp, learn who is coming, and inspect their gear. A sword stolen from a sleeping knight will be missing when the fight begins, while poison in the well will weaken the whole party. Set traps along the road, gather herbs, brew poisons, mine ore, and forge the weapon you need. The next day begins only when you decide to end the night.

At dawn, the heroes take to the road. Traps and poisons thin their ranks, but anyone who survives the journey must be faced at the entrance to your lair. Let too many enemies through and the run ends.

After the fight, take weapons, armor, and other items from the fallen heroes. Keep what you need and sacrifice the rest at the altar. The Dark Energy you receive unlocks night talents and new ways to prepare for later raids. The enemies grow stronger with each day.

In the game:

  • Night preparation with no time limit

  • Camp scouting and equipment theft from future opponents

  • Traps and poisons that affect the next raid

  • Six classes with subclasses and their own skills

  • Nine equipment slots and hundreds of items

  • Runes, essences, and set bonuses

  • Herbalism, alchemy, mining, and smithing

  • Night talents purchased with Dark Energy

  • Velmor, a dark fantasy world seen from the monsters' side

A Hacker-Noir Logic Deduction Game with Real Depth

Unlimited, freshly generated puzzles. A genuine 10-level difficulty curve. And a solver-verified guarantee that every case has exactly one solution and can be completed through pure logic, with no guessing required.

Mark each grid cell True or False and uncover the single solution hidden in the clues. Prefer a daily ritual? Every player worldwide receives the same Daily Case each day: solve it once, then wait until tomorrow for the next mystery.

Three Ways to Play, Three Grid Sizes

Case Files

The main mode offers unlimited practice across 4x4 and 5x5 grids, plus a 10-level Difficulty Ladder. Progress from straightforward introductory clues to the Master tier, featuring a rare cardinality challenge: "Exactly two of the following three statements are true." You will also encounter adjacency clues, including deductions about which items are immediately next to one another. Each tier introduces a new reasoning method rather than simply increasing the puzzle size, creating a genuine sense of progression.

Enable Overclocked to remove utility items and add a countdown timer. It is designed for players who want to solve under pressure instead of taking their time.

Weekly Case

Take on a more challenging shared case each week, with puzzles scaling up to a 6x6 grid. Additional Revives give you more room to recover from mistakes.

Daily Case

A quick shared ritual: one 4x4 puzzle, one attempt, and the same case for everyone worldwide.

Four Tools for Difficult Moments

Each case includes four tools, with one use of each:

* Scanner reveals a cell.

* Polygraph identifies mistakes on the current grid.

* Clarify highlights the row or column connected to an unused clue.

* Revive removes one incorrect final submission so you can continue instead of losing the case.

These tools are designed as safety nets, not shortcuts. Weekly Cases include additional Revives.

Every Case Is Verified

Cases are generated fresh and without limits. Before a puzzle becomes available, it is checked to ensure that it has exactly one solution and can be completed through logical deduction rather than guessing.

You will never receive an unsolvable case or a puzzle with multiple valid answers. If you get stuck, the solution is always contained within the clues.

Five Distinct Case Packs

Investigate five original case packs, each with its own visual style and fictional terminal:

* Corporate espionage.

* Rogue surveillance.

* Deepfake fraud.

* Ransomware.

* The original Cyber-Heist.

The same detective and deduction engine connect every pack. These are not five separate stories, but five different terminals to investigate.

A Gallery Worth Chasing

Earn commendations across eleven separate tracks, with real medal artwork and fifty total tiers. Tracks cover the Daily Case, Weekly Case, Case Files, Overclocked mode, five dedicated 5x5 mastery paths, and the Campaign.

Every locked tier is visible from the beginning, so you always know what you are working toward. A complete Statistics screen tracks streaks and solve times across every mode.

Clues That Actually Get More Interesting

The difficulty curve begins with direct facts, then introduces:

* Ordinal clues about item order.

* Adjacency clues about neighboring items.

* Either/or statements.

* If-then logic.

* Cardinality clues requiring you to determine how many statements are true.

This is a real progression in reasoning, not simply a series of larger grids.

Fully Localized in 14 Languages

The game supports:

* English.

* Simplified Chinese.

* Japanese.

* Korean.

* Russian.

* Spanish.

* German.

* French.

* Polish.

* Brazilian Portuguese.

* Turkish.

* Ukrainian.

* Italian.

* Indonesian.

Every clue required to solve a case is translated, not just the menus and interface.

Designed to Be Inclusive

True and False are always distinguished by shape as well as color, making the game safer for colorblind players.

Share codes let you send friends the exact Case Files puzzle you solved.

If you want deep deduction and long-term progression, start with the Case Files Difficulty Ladder. If you prefer a quick shared challenge, return each day for the Daily Case.

[Game Overview]

The Guidelines : Hotel Napoli is a horror observation simulation that combines a Napolitan-style horror manual with a CCTV surveillance system.

From a surveillance room cut off from the outside world, analyze recorded CCTV footage overlooking the hidden corners of the hotel and maintain your composure as the environment slowly begins to change.

Observe the hotel as it changes little by little each day, find anomalies, and report them correctly according to the hotel's manual. As the days repeat, memories of the past and the strange events taking place in the hotel slowly begin to connect.

[Key Features]

  • Observe the CCTV and find anomalies.

Check the CCTV cameras installed throughout the hotel and look for anomalies. Something may disappear, something that wasn't there before may appear, or a familiar space may subtly change. Correctly report the anomalies you discover.

  • Follow the hotel's manual.

There are rules that must be followed in the hotel. Determine what you have discovered through the CCTV and follow the instructions written in the manual. But be warned. At some point, the rules you thought you knew may begin to differ from reality. A wrong report or failure to follow the rules may lead to unexpected consequences.

  • Face the truth within the repeating days.

Each day at the hotel repeats itself. A single incorrect report will send you back to the first day. As time repeats, the strange events taking place in the hotel and memories of your past slowly begin to form a single story. Discover what happened here, and why you came to this place.

Explore an immersive steampunk laboratory.

Solve ingenious puzzles woven into the environment and the story.

Environment and object interactions.

Unravel the dark secret behind Voss's experiments.

And more quality of life features, such as systems for inventory, diaries, and dynamic hints.

Getting to school should be easy. Not when your school is at the top of the world.

The Highest School: Don’t Look Down is a vertical climbing adventure where a simple trip to school becomes an insane journey through time.

Your destination is waiting somewhere far above. There are no shortcuts, no elevators, and no easy way up.

You just have to keep climbing.

Begin your journey in the Ancient World and climb your way through different eras of human history. The higher you go, the more the world changes around you — new architecture, environments, characters, obstacles, and challenges await in every era.

Scale ancient ruins, cross pirate wrecks, climb through the Wild West, conquer the modern world, and push even higher toward the future.

Anything can become your next step.

Jump across buildings, vehicles, ruins, machines, floating structures, and whatever else you can find to gain a little more height.

But be careful.

There are no checkpoints waiting to save you after every difficult jump. One mistake can send you falling hundreds of meters — through places and entire eras you already conquered.

The school is waiting at the top.

The only question is...

Can you reach it?

CLIMB THROUGH TIME.

REACH THE SCHOOL.

DON’T LOOK DOWN.

The house is dark. Your flashlight is dying.

Something laughs in the ballroom beneath Grisewood Manor. You have a pistol, a failing flashlight, and however many rooms you can survive on the way down.

THE HOUSE ON GRISEWOOD is a top-down gothic horror shooter about limited light and limited resources. Every room is black until you sweep it. Walls swallow your beam, corners hide what's waiting, and the battery counting down in your hand is the only reason you can see at all.

Light is a resource

Your flashlight carves a narrow cone through the dark, and it does not last forever. Switch it off to save power and the manor closes in around you. Leave it on and you will be blind when it matters. Batteries are scavenged, never guaranteed.

Every shot is a decision

Six rounds in the revolver and a slow reload. A shotgun if you find one, and shells if you're lucky. Ammunition is scarce enough that running is often smarter than fighting — and knowing which is which is the difference between life and death.

The things in the dark are not all the same

Shamblers press forward without stopping. Grinners lunge from beyond your light. Weepers freeze in your beam and move the instant it leaves them. Something tall breathes in rooms you haven't reached yet. Learn what each one does, or learn the hard way.

Descend

Nineteen rooms of a rotting manor — library, chapel, conservatory, crypt — connected in ways that don't always make sense. Find your way down to the ballroom and end what's laughing there.

ZOMBIE SURVIVAL MODE

Sealed inside the Grand Hall with the doors boarded shut. Waves arrive out of the black and never stop coming. Scavenge rounds, batteries and bandages from supply caches scattered across the floor — which means leaving the corner you're hiding in. Survive as long as you can, then go again.

OUT NOW | Single-player | About 2 hours | First-person psychological horror

ABOUT THIS GAME

The Ice is Watching is a first-person psychological horror experience that plunges you into a desolate, frozen nightmare. You don't play as a hero. You play as a desperate woman driven by a single question: Where is he?

Tracing your lover's last known location to a remote mountain cabin, the temperature drops and a chilling realization sets in: you are not alone. A looming figure known only as "The Ice" is here. And he's been expecting you.

BREAK THE CYCLE

Your journey begins in the artificial warmth of a city hotel, fueled by social media clues and fragile hope. But as the rain turns to blinding snow and the road vanishes into white nothingness, hope shatters.

You reach the cabin only to find your escape sabotaged: the battery is gone, the tires are missing. You are no longer the seeker; you are the next target for a frozen collection. To break the cycle, you must face the stalker who watches from the pine tree shadows.

SURVIVE THE NIGHT

Seen through an immersive first-person view, the core experience focuses on survival, heat management, and stealth.

Thermal Survival. The cold is your primary enemy. Manage your body heat by scavenging firewood and keeping the hearth alive.

Unpredictable Stalker AI. The Ice, a mysterious and terrifying cowboy, is no scripted jumpscare. He observes, stalks, and hunts dynamically based on your noise and movement.

Environmental Puzzles. Scavenge for vehicle parts to make your escape while navigating psychological traps and deciphering chilling audio logs.

KEY FEATURES

  • Atmospheric Terror: The vast, suffocating scale of the snowy wilderness contrasted with the claustrophobic dread of a cabin hiding dark secrets.
  • Body Heat Mechanics: Feel the frost. As your temperature drops, your vision blurs, your movement falters, and the world turns into a lethal hallucination.
  • The Frozen Gallery: Uncover the tragic fate of the Frozen Lover, a symbolic narrative exploring obsession and eternal preservation.
  • Immersive 3D Audio: High-quality sound design where every creaking floorboard or whisper of wind serves as your only warning. Headphones recommended.
  • A Concise Nightmare: A focused, story-driven horror experience designed to be finished in one sitting (approx. 2 hours), leaving a lingering chill.
  • Gritty Western Aesthetics: A unique visual style combining the rugged edge of a dark Western with the cold, sterile beauty of an arctic grave.

The fire is dying. The Ice is watching. Keep the hearth alive.

about_html:
You are trapped inside an enormous furniture store whose aisles seem to continue forever. During the day, the store is quiet enough to explore, gather supplies and prepare a place to survive. When the lights go out, the employees become hostile—and they begin searching.

SURVIVE THE DAY AND NIGHT

Use the daylight to search display rooms, departments and storage areas for food, water and useful materials. Prepare carefully before night arrives and turns the store into a far more dangerous place.

EXPLORE AN ENDLESS STORE

Travel through a procedurally generated world filled with furniture displays, interconnected departments, unusual rooms and rare landmarks. Fog conceals the distant aisles, so you never know what may be waiting beyond the next department.

SCAVENGE, CRAFT AND BUILD

Collect furniture, tools and materials from around the store. Craft useful equipment and turn what you find into shelter and protection. Different materials have different properties, so your choices affect the usefulness and durability of what you create.

AVOID THE EMPLOYEES

The employees may appear harmless during the day, but darkness changes their behaviour. Hide, escape or defend yourself while managing your limited resources and trying to survive until morning.

KEY FEATURES

• An endless procedurally generated furniture store
• A day-and-night survival cycle
• Hostile employees that hunt after dark
• Hunger, thirst and resource management
• Scavenging, crafting and base building
• Exploration, stealth and first-person combat
• Rare rooms and landmarks to discover
• A single-player survival-horror experience

Write words. Fill shelves. Watch reality buckle.

Words become pages. Pages become books. Every book needs a genre, and each genre changes how your library grows. Fill enough shelves and reality folds. Everything resets.

Almost. You rebuild faster, stranger, deeper. And the Library starts to notice you've been here before.

Prestige is the story

Tooltips change between runs. Labels rename themselves. Log entries reference books you haven't written yet.

Five acts. Three endings. One Library that remembers everything.

Core Features

12 Genres, Your Strategy

Horror builds a Dread meter toward devastating bursts. Poetry grants timed global buffs. Romance generates paired words. Your genre balance shapes your path to the ending.

80+ Secret Combinations

Rare Words surface as you write. Combine them into Phrases with powerful effects — none documented. No guide tells you what "Eternal Autobiography Tome" does.

Five Prestige Tiers

Redraft resets your town. Rewrite resets the county. Redaction resets the country. Each tier brings new currencies, new mechanics, and new cracks in the fourth wall.

The Interface Changes Around You

No cutscenes. The story lives in the menus, names that shift between runs, entries that shouldn't exist yet, a Library that speaks through your UI.

Designed to End

~30-50 hours. Three resolution paths. Optional postgame. Complete experience, not a live service.

Also Includes

  • Scriptorium - merge Words into higher-rarity discoveries

  • Skill tree with three progression branches

  • Genre synergy bonuses

  • Offline progression (up to 24 hours, expandable)

  • Active play multiplier (3-5x idle rate)

  • Run history and stats

  • No ads. No microtransactions. Just the Library.

From Endpaper

Endpaper is one person in South West UK, building the kind of incremental I always wanted to find: one that ends, one that means something, one where the systems are the story. Built in Godot 4.6.

The script has been carefully written, refined, and localized, with a total length of around 40,000–50,000 words.

The story is kept tight and intentional, with every joke and detail carefully polished for the English version. It's more focused than a TV drama, and more complete than a film.

Over the course of 5–6 hours, every moment is worth your time.

This is a story that mixes comedy with more grounded, emotional moments.

It’s light in tone at times, but also deals with quiet, sincere feelings about life and change.

All in-game text is fully voiced—from narration to every character line.

With 26 background tracks and over 300 ambient sound effects, we hope the island feels alive, especially when played with headphones.

From beaches, caves, a lighthouse, flower fields, wheat fields, to local festivals, the world is shown across different times of day.

Every corner is crafted to reflect the charm of this small island just a few dozen kilometers away from the mainland.

Beyond their personalities, we focused on giving each character rich facial expressions.

These details enhance the storytelling and highlight each character’s charm in conversation.

1985. Your friend never came home.

Billy's bike is at the gates. Something moves beyond the fog. You go in anyway.

A Horror Puzzle Built From the Inside Out.

There are no weapons. There is only hiding, running, and thinking.

Designed by escape-room enthusiasts and mystery obsessives, The Kharzov Effect is a

first-person horror puzzle set at the fog-drenched Oregon estate of Dr. Kharzov.

 

First-person stealth horror — navigate the grounds without a weapon. Your only tools are your wits, your patience, and the shadows.

Monsters with distinct detection — some see you. Some hear you. Some feel you. Solving the estate and surviving it are the same problem.

 Escape-room-style environmental puzzles — every locked door, every sealed room has an answer hidden in the world around you. No hand-holding. 

Atmospheric environments — a world designed to keep you guessing. BTW, do you like analog horror? 

Period-accurate details from the 80's — before the internet. Before mobile phones. Before anyone would believe you. Just you, the dark, and whatever Kharzov built in there.

 Layered narrative mystery — the puzzles are part of the story. The deeper you go, the bigger the lore.

Meta gaming & ARG-inspired mystery — a hidden thread built entirely 

from easter eggs that transcends the game itself. Find it if you can.

English • Chinese • German • French • Portuguese • Japanese • Korean • Russian • Polish • Spanish

Doorway Studios wanted to build something that didn't exist yet — Traditional scares weren't enough — we wanted puzzles that challenge your mind, lore that rewards curiosity, stealth that makes you sweat, and moments that make you question whether the game is playing you.

The Kharzov Effect is the first chapter of an unfolding story. Chapter 2 is already in active development.

Add to your Wishlist to be notified the moment The Kharzov Effect releases.

Join our Discord!   

Streamers & creators: streaming and monetized videos are welcome, no permission needed. Original music and CC0 sound effects, so we will never claim your videos. Full guidelines in our press kit.
