about_html:
Turn-based fleet battles in open space, with no grid. Ships move freely, and both fleets share one turn order set by speed. Asteroids block shots along their actual shape, and a ship in the line of fire takes the hit meant for the one behind it. Ships outside your radar cannot be targeted. Hover any target to see the hit chance and damage before you commit.

Your own Alliance never fired a shot at you. It simply stopped sending convoys. So you break away with four ships and fight inward to the galactic core. The Sehn crossed the dark between galaxies to take it. You are going to put them back in the dark.

WHAT YOU DECIDE EACH TURN

  • Act now, or hold a ship's turn until the end of the round.
  • Split your move around your shots: slip out, fire, get back behind the rock.
  • Fire blind at a radar contact, or put a Scout's radar on it for full damage.
  • Shoot a glowing vein asteroid instead of an enemy. It pays out the moment it breaks.
  • Spend a fleet-wide Admiral Order. You bring four into each battle, and each works once.

SHOVE THEM INTO SOMETHING WORSE

Gravity weapons, tractor beams and grappling hooks drag or shove ships into minefields, storms and black holes. Most worlds set one battle rule for both fleets, like volcanic heat that feeds fire weapons. In one of the 22 battle objectives, a supergun charges for five rounds, then one-shots your flagship.

EVERY FLEET YOU BREAK PAYS FOR THE NEXT ONE



You start with Alliance hulls and no faction pick. Wins pay out blueprints and gear, previewed on the map before you warp. Beat a faction's fleets to build its hulls. Each of the 85 hulls has its own ability: a Pirate Frigate lays mines, and your Reaper Scouts raise the dead as ghosts that fight for you. The Hive fights without shields and regrows, and Wraith stay cloaked until they fire.



Fit ships from 81 modules, including drones and a Barrier Wall your fleet fires through but enemies cannot cross. At levels 5, 10, 15 and 20 each ship picks one of two perks, and many change a rule, not a number. By the time you reach the core, you will not be four ships.

TAKE TERRITORY. HOLD WHAT YOU CLAIM.



Each run is one of four sectors, from the rim to the core: a freshly generated map that ends at a boss stronghold. The first ends at Greywall, where Admiral Edric Vance sent your convoys. Take a world and build on it: a Salvage Depot whose drones strip the wrecks you leave mid-battle, or Reverse Time, which undoes one fleet wipe per run. The enemy stronghold strikes back at your frontline world, with three warps of warning.

LOSE THE RUN. KEEP THE FLEET.

In the campaign, a run ends only when every ship you brought into a battle is destroyed, you abandon it, or you take the sector's stronghold and open the next one. Retreat, or lose a fight with ships still standing, and the run goes on.

When it ends, the map and your ship and module levels reset. You keep every ship you own, even the destroyed ones, with the perks each one earned, plus your modules, blueprints, Admiral Orders and every Commander upgrade you have bought. Clear the campaign and your fleet carries on into Campaign Endless.

BY THE NUMBERS

  • Ships from 14 factions in one fleet
  • 85 hulls in 7 ship classes
  • 81 modules, 47 ship perks, 23 Admiral Orders
  • 22 battle objectives on 49 world types
  • 27 buildings and 17 Commander upgrade trees
  • 4 campaign sectors and 2 Endless modes

Made by one developer, Brandon, at Pizza Pizza Games.

THE LAST ROUTE HOME

You return from a distant transport run to find an invasion already underway. Communications are jammed. The inner worlds have not been warned. One ship now stands between the hostile armada and Prima Verd.

The Last Bastion: Beyond the Frontier is a story-driven vertical space shooter built around a campaign of ten increasingly dangerous frontiers. Fight your way inward, restore the communications network, and assemble a ship capable of reaching the source of the enemy command signal.

THE ENEMY WILL NOT SIMPLY FLY AT YOU

Hostile ships enter from multiple directions, reposition in flight, launch flanking attacks, form manoeuvring groups, and cover one another. Rammers lock onto your course, minelayers restrict your space, teleporters change position, and repair vessels return damaged targets to the fight.

Every new frontier expands the enemy arsenal and increases the pressure. Difficulty grows through overlapping threats, faster projectiles, denser formations, and more aggressive attack patterns — not health bars alone.

COMMANDERS CHANGE THE RULES OF THE FIGHT

Heavy ships are not enlarged versions of ordinary enemies. They unfold armour sections, detach weapons, construct firing networks, protect vulnerable systems, and transition through multiple phases during combat.

Read each attack through mechanical movement and light signals, find your window to strike, and survive the commander blockades before facing the flagship of each frontier.

BUILD A SHIP AROUND YOUR STYLE

Develop your ship across a nine-step mastery track. Core upgrades steadily unlock its full potential, while four pairs of mutually exclusive specialisations let you shape your preferred style: control, explosive damage, penetration, shrapnel, the Chronosphere, or point defence.

Purchase twelve ship modules across three technology tiers, combine them with your skills, and unlock additional synergies. Enemy strength never scales secretly to match your equipment — every upgrade delivers a real, measurable advantage.

THE BREAKTHROUGH IS MORE THAN A STRAIGHT FIGHT

The sector map connects the main campaign, trading hubs, and optional operations. Navigate the hazardous approach to Tartassa, restore the Lost Relay, and expose camouflaged hostiles hidden among civilian traffic over Erynia.

Side missions reveal new routes and technology, provide valuable credits, and help prepare your ship for the next stage of the pursuit — without replacing the skill required in the main battles.

ASTRA MAINTAINS THE SHIPBOARD ARCHIVE

ASTRA is the Autonomous System for Tactical Response and Analysis. It warns you of incoming threats, reconstructs intercepted signals, and studies technology recovered from the wreckage of enemy commanders.

Every new archive entry adds another piece to the invasion. The closer you get to Prima Verd, the clearer it becomes: the armada has come for more than a single world, and what you recover may prove more important than conventional weapons.

REACH THE HEART OF THE ARMADA

Ten story frontiers transform a desperate border breakthrough into a full-scale pursuit of the enemy command source. The final route tests everything you have built in a battle against Hyperion, a five-phase flagship.

Commander checkpoints preserve the pace of longer sorties, while full controller support lets you navigate the sector map, shops, mastery tree, minigames, and combat missions without a mouse.

KEY FEATURES

·       10 story-driven combat frontiers with steadily escalating intensity.

·       Multi-phase commanders and flagships with individual attacks and transformations.

·       9 mastery steps, 4 pairs of specialisations, and the option to rebuild your chosen branches.

·       12 ship modules across 3 technology tiers, supported by a separate synergy system.

·       A sector map with side operations, minigames, shops, and a shipboard archive.

·       Transparent balancing with no hidden enemy scaling based on build strength.

·       Full keyboard and controller support.

The 17th year of Chongzhen. The capital has fallen.

The Liaodong frontier is lost. Beyond the pass, the living flee and the dead are left behind. Deserters, singing girls, Taoist priests, wandering healers—a rabble of those who can no longer stay, cobble together a company marching south.

  • Turn-Based Formation Combat: Position your ranks, time your blocks, shift your ground—every move may be someone's last.

  • Twelve Exiles: Each has their own past, temper, and ties. They will be wounded, broken, scarred—and some will die forever, their names etched into the Roll of the Departed.

  • Camps & the Road of Exile: Pitch camp, ration food, assign night watches; chart your route across the map, through blizzards, plague, and pursuing foes.

  • Stress & Morale: Wounds cut flesh, but also the spirit. Anxiety, fear, and collapse will show themselves in the thick of battle.

  • Ink-Wash Woodcut Art: A hand-painted, dark monochrome style—the sky over the late Ming never once brightened.

  • Multiple Endings: Yunnan or Quanzhou—will you fight for a slim chance at life, or abandon your homeland forever?

The Last Helm

Opening a shop is easy.

The hard part is keeping it afloat when everyone wants something at the exact same time.

*The Last Helm* is a trading and management game where you build and run your very own shop in a fantasy world.

Start with a small shop, purchase goods, craft your own items, hire employees, and expand your business over time.

Of course, things won't always go according to plan. The cashier might slack off somewhere, sales might stall because your hauler is constantly running back and forth to the storage room, or you might completely run out of stock right when you need it most.

Oh well, that's all part of management.

Start Small

You won't have much space, gold, or inventory in the beginning. You'll start with just a few shelves, a small storage room, and a handful of items to sell.

Expand your shop as you earn.

Unlock new rooms, place shelves and displays, organize your storage, and design your shop's interior to fit your workflow.

Layout matters too. Because you don't want your employees spending their entire day sprinting from one end of the shop to the other.

You Decide What to Sell

You don't have to buy every product premade.

Set up a blacksmith workshop to craft swords, shields, and armor; or construct an alchemy station to brew potions and concoctions.

Focus on trade by buying and reselling goods, invest in production to manufacture your own items, or do both.

Some of the items you can sell:

* Swords, shields, and armor

* Potions and alchemy products

* Raw materials

* Everyday items

* Various trade goods

Good Staff, Great Shop

After a while, trying to do everything yourself won't be such a bright idea.

Hire haulers, cashiers, cleaners, blacksmiths, alchemists, and researchers.

Each employee has unique skills and traits. Assigning the right person to the right job can dramatically change how smoothly your store runs.

Level up your workers, keep their morale high, and try to make sure everyone knows what they're supposed to be doing.

Because eight people heading to the same storage room at once usually isn't great organization.

Step Outside

Stepping out of the shop to explore is also part of the job.

Dispatch your explorers into unknown lands to gather rare raw materials and special resources.

Instead of buying certain resources, you can find them yourself. Though you'll have to wait for your explorers to make it back.

Hopefully, they do.

Use the resources gathered from your expeditions to unlock new products, crafting stations, and employee perks in the research tree.

No Two Days Are the Same

What your customers want today might not be the same tomorrow.

One day everyone is looking for a new sword, and the next day your potions might sell out instantly. Keep an eye on the market, restock on time, and set competitive prices.

Special event days can throw a wrench in things too.

When a knight regiment arrives in town, armor sales might spike. When an alchemy festival begins, suddenly everyone is after potions.

If you're prepared, great.

If not... your shelves might be left a bit empty.

How Will You Run Your Shop?

In *The Last Helm*, there is no single right way to play.

Focus heavily on crafting, double down on trading, or gradually build a massive shop that combines both.

Will you spend your money on hiring staff?

A new crafting bench?

Or fitting just a few more shelves into your shop?

The choice is yours.

After all, it's your shop.

Just don't yell at the cashier.

It's probably not their fault.

The Last Lunch is a first-person psychological cooking horror game set in a post-Soviet school. You play as a new cafeteria worker: prepare meals, complete your everyday duties, and make it through five working days while gradually discovering that something unsettling lies beneath the ordinary routine.

Work in the School Cafeteria

Each shift begins with seemingly ordinary work. Prepare different meals, use kitchen equipment and ingredients, and complete the tasks assigned to you throughout the day.

Cooking and cafeteria work are a central part of the gameplay rather than just a backdrop to the story.

Explore the School and Its Surroundings

Your life is not limited to the kitchen. Explore the school and the surrounding neighborhood, interact with characters, visit different locations, and pay attention to details that may reveal more about what is happening around you.

Experience a Story Unfolding Over Five Days

Each new working day moves the story forward. Listen to radio broadcasts, talk to people, notice changes in your surroundings, and piece together clues as the familiar routine gradually becomes more unsettling.

A seemingly ordinary job soon becomes connected to a disturbing mystery.

Key Features

  • First-person cooking and cafeteria gameplay

  • A story unfolding over five working days

  • Exploration of a post-Soviet school and its surrounding neighborhood

  • Character interactions and environmental storytelling

  • Radio broadcasts, conversations, and other clues that develop the mystery

  • Psychological horror focused on atmosphere and tension rather than constant action

  • A detailed post-Soviet setting inspired by everyday life, architecture, and school environments

NEW MATCH!

You wake up on a beautiful Saturday morning and open a dating app on your phone. As you browse through the profiles, a mysterious woman catches your attention. In her photos, she appears warm, cheerful, and perfect. But when you finally meet her, you notice a disturbing difference between the person you saw on the screen and the woman standing before you.

What begins as an ordinary date gradually turns into a dark and dangerous night. You must face the consequences of your decisions, follow the clues around you, and uncover the truth behind this unsettling situation.

FEATURES

  • A story-driven, first-person psychological horror experience

  • A mysterious story that begins through a dating app

  • An atmosphere of escalating tension as the hours pass

  • Dark secrets uncovered by carefully exploring your surroundings

  • Decisions that affect the course of the game

She looked perfect in her profile. But some people are not who they appear to be on the screen.

TONIGHT COULD BE YOUR LAST MATCH!

Survive the Abandoned Baku Metro

Explore abandoned metro stations, navigate dark tunnels, scavenge for supplies, and fight to escape the nightmare beneath the city.

Fight. Explore. Survive.

Face terrifying creatures, manage limited resources, solve puzzles, and uncover the mystery behind the outbreak.

  • First-person Survival Horror

  • Resource Management

  • Puzzle Solving

  • Atmospheric Exploration

Every Station Has a Story

Travel through iconic Baku Metro stations. Discover hidden notes, historical references, forgotten memories, and disturbing secrets hidden throughout the Baku Metro.

Your Choices Matter

Every decision has consequences.

The fog has changed everything.

An old train has stopped at the edge of an infected sector. People are disappearing beyond the electrical perimeter, fragments of alien messages can be heard from the radio, and the automated MELISSA system continues to broadcast warnings, the meaning of which is becoming increasingly disturbing.

The engineer lives alone on the train and tries not to remember what happened before. But one day, a girl named Mia appears within the perimeter. She claims to be uninfected and asks for help.

Can she be trusted?

And can you trust your own memories?

The Last Train is an atmospheric story-driven game with elements of visual novel, exploration, and survival. You will explore the old train and surrounding areas, search for supplies, read diary entries, make decisions, and gradually reconstruct the events of the past.

FEATURES

  • Gloomy post-Soviet atmosphere.

  • Non-linear storyline and decisions with consequences.

  • Explore the train and abandoned locations.

  • Character relationship system.

  • A diary with entries, a map, items, and discovered clues.

  • Hand-drawn scenes, animations, and atmospheric sound design.

  • A story about memory, guilt, loneliness, and the struggle to maintain one's humanity.

  • Sometimes the worst things aren't just outside the perimeter.

The Story: A Hero Lost in Time

The year is 1928, but not the one you know. You are Hugo, commander of the LZ-128, a top-secret German Zeppelin trapped in a parallel dimension. In a desperate act of heroism, you detonated a Zero-Point charge to seal the rift, saving Earth from a reptilian invasion—but at a terrible cost. Now, you and your crew are stranded in a hostile universe ruled by cold-blooded overlords.

"You are the last Zeppelin, Hugo. Save humanity." — Admiral v. Schreck

The Gameplay: Classic Arcade Action

The Last Zeppelin is a retro-inspired 2D shooter that prioritizes pure, addictive gameplay. With simple, intuitive controls, it’s easy to pick up but a challenge to survive as the reptilian hordes grow stronger with every level.

  • Retro Combat: Simple movement and firing mechanics. No complicated combos—just aim and survive.

  • Zero-Energy Arsenal: When standard bullets aren't enough, unleash Zero-Energy Ammo or the Zero-Energy Impulse to cut the attackers' strength in half.

  • Manage Your Power: Watch your gauges! Special weapons require at least 20% zero-energy level to function. Use them wisely or find yourself defenseless.

The Enemies: Reptilian Might

Battle through waves of bizarre and deadly foes from the reptiloid war machine:

  • Vintage Airmen: Dogfight against reptilian biplanes and the legendary Reptilian Red Barons.

  • Anachronistic Tech: Dodge fire from advanced Jet Fighters and the mysterious Flying Saucers.

  • Prehistoric Terror: Take down armored Pterosaurs equipped with specialized weaponry.

  • The Fleet: Engage massive Reptilian Zeppelins in high-stakes aerial combat.

  • Bonus Missions: After each successful battle, you can infiltrate a Reptilian Tower-Fortress to search for secret egg-incubation chambers

Bonus Content

Want to know how Hugo ended up in the rift? This game includes a summary of the prequel story. For the full experience, the complete prequel audiobook is available for free on YouTube!

You Are Not the Real Heiress.

But everyone must believe you are.

Every lie could be the one that gives you away.

♡ WISHLIST NOW — DON'T LET THEM FIND OUT.

1. Background settings

"Lies are my spear, my shield, and the glass slippers under my feet."

You grew up in an orphanage, and your "brother" An Cha helped you plan a package swap - you became the wealthy daughter who was supposed to die in an accident. From an orphan girl to a rich and beautiful girl, every step is on the edge of a knife. Fiancé Zhou Hejing is gentle and gentle, but he asks you for every flaw you have. An Cha is not related to you, but he reaches out for you every time you almost reveal your secret. You have to plunder, be plundered, deceive, and be deceived - darkness is inevitable, but redemption may not be possible.

2. Core gameplay

1. Three-dimensional attribute development system

Character attributes: Your choices affect the initial attitude of others towards you in social situations, and also create your character.

Favorability: Determines how many traps you can spot in conspiracy conversations and whether you can reverse the situation.

Suspicion value: It accumulates every time you tell a lie. If it is too high, it will cause the character's psychological collapse or logical loopholes. If it is too low, it will be impossible to maintain the identity.

2. Multi-layered favorability and hidden relationship network

The plot development of each main character has a favorability value and is also affected by a suspicion value.

Overt favor can be accumulated through choices, but dark trust can only be accumulated through actions that are in line with the character's true interests.

Your choices may change the balance of power between characters, which in turn affects the direction of the subsequent plot.

3. Featured system

The achievement system has more than 50 built-in achievements, covering plot milestones, attribute challenges and hidden easter eggs. All achievements can unlock developer messages and original paintings. Favorite character rankings, ranked based on player votes. Lie Notes contains props and key terms in the adventure. The collection progress is linked to achievements. If you collect 100%, you can get clues to the hidden ending.

The entire game contains more than twelve official endings, as well as several unexpected endings, all of which are automatically generated by the real-time accumulation of variables. The same choice may lead to completely different fates in different weeks - because every lie you tell rewrites the underlying logic of the story.

You do not know where you are.

You do not know when it is.

When you open your eyes, the only thing you realize is this:

The living inside this place are already dead.

The Lifeline is a first person survival horror game set in a dark and abandoned hospital.

As the player, your goal is to find a way out of the hospital, survive against zombies, and overcome the dangers you encounter. While exploring the hospital corridors, patient rooms, and closed areas, you will use weapons, watch out for traps, and react quickly to unexpected attacks.

The game includes exploration, zombie encounters, weapon use, close danger moments, quick reaction scenes, a tense sound atmosphere, and survival focused gameplay.

With every step, the line between life and death becomes thinner.

Hunting zombies is not as easy as you think.

Stomp deeper before the match burns out

The Little Stomping Girl combines automatic stomp mining with strategic equipment placement. Gather resources, create your own build, and descend deeper underground.

No constant clicking required. Simply point your cursor where you want to mine, and the girl will hop and stomp across nearby tiles. Collect minerals and equipment while the match burns, then prepare for your next descent.

Arrange your equipment and discover stronger combinations

Fit equipment of different shapes and sizes into a limited grid. Place items next to each other for bonus effects, and upgrade equipment slots to boost their stats. Expand your equipment grid and bag to try even more combinations.

Even equipment of the same type can have different bonuses and stats. Combine your latest finds with your skills to create your own way to mine.

Turn little stomps into powerful chain reactions

Develop your stomps through a skill tree with 146 nodes. Combine shards, echoes, and clones with dynamite, fireworks, and lightning to unleash chain reactions that shake the underground.

As your build grows stronger, a single match lets you smash more tiles and bring back greater rewards.

Collect unique equipment and unlock the power of your collection

Discover 297 unique equipment items, each with its own special effects. Every discovery becomes part of your collection.

Unlock display stands as you descend deeper, and activate the unique effects of collected equipment without using equipment grid space. Combine the effects of equipped and displayed items to create new builds.

about_html:
Master the Art of Farming in This Active Incremental Experience

Manage 8 unique scenarios, each focused on a different part of a chicken farm. Start with a small rural farm and progress toward the most advanced industrial production systems. Raise chicks, incubate eggs, automate processes, and discover many more ways to grow your poultry empire.

  • Challenges & Replayability: Each scenario includes its own challenges to test your strategy and keep the experience fresh.

  • Endless Mode: Keep optimizing, producing, and expanding your farm even after completing the main objectives.

Community-Backed & Player-Tested

The prototype of the first scenario was rigorously tested within gaming communities, with outstanding results:

  • 4.7 / 5 stars on Itch.io, based on over 475 ratings.

  • Highest-rated game on IncrementalDB (284 positive / 19 negative).

As an industrial security agent, you have been tasked with infiltrating a factory that was abruptly shut down a few years ago to retrieve important technical documents and escape safely.

You will proceed with the mission following in the footsteps of the missing advance team. Overcome the instinctive human fear of the unknown brought by darkness, secure the documents deep within the pitch-black factory, and escape this place safely.

Search and Escape

You must search the factory, retrieve the technical documents, and escape without being discovered by 'Him'. However, 'He' will not simply let you walk out with the documents intact. Make sure to complete the mission and discover the story of this place. This will not be an ordinary factory.

'Him'

'Him' roams throughout the factory, and the moment he spots you, he will charge at you with an axe. His speed changes with each playthrough, and he wanders the factory at random rather than following a fixed route, so you never know when or where you might run into him. Always stay alert and watch your surroundings.

Terminal

Utilize the terminal provided to aid your mission. Check your mission objectives and receive instructions from headquarters. View the factory map to find your way, acquire hidden security codes, enter the factory's systems, and disable the security. However, it is not omnipotent, so if a problem occurs, you may sometimes have to solve it yourself.

Flashlight

In this pitch-black factory, where you cannot see even a step ahead, the flashlight will probably be almost your only means of seeing. It has no battery limit, so you can use it throughout the mission. You can also adjust its brightness. However, if you shine it on 'Him', or if he sees its light, he will come looking for you.

CCTV

You can check the CCTVs scattered throughout the factory using the monitors in the manager's office. Use them to track 'His' movements and routes, allowing you to move safely. However, this feature cannot be utilized if the factory loses power.

There are no safe zones in this factory. From the moment you begin your mission, you may encounter danger anywhere, at any time.

Survive this extreme darkness, safely retrieve the technical documents, and complete the mission you have been assigned.

Good luck.

Welcome to the friendliest street in the world. Also the most dishonest.


White picket fences. Trimmed lawns. Mailboxes painted to match every house. And somewhere on this cul-de-sac, somebody who spends their nights burying bombs in the neighbors' gardens.

The Neighborhood Liars is social deduction and card bluffing for 4 to 12 people. You get two cards, two hearts, and absolutely no obligation to tell the truth.

The neighbors are twelve automata: enamelled tin robots with a screen for a face, each with their own head and hat, painted in their player’s color. They walk like wind-up toys, sit on a stool at the plaza table, point at the accused with the whole arm and talk with their screens — the mouth is the wave of your voice. (Prefer the classic beans? They’re in Options.)

Every match opens with the whole table watching the neighborhood from the sky together, each neighbor's name lighting up over their house. Then comes a card only you can see: citizen or impostor — and if you're an impostor, who your accomplices are and how many of you sit at the table.

Say anything. Prove nothing.


On your turn your robot walks itself across the street to the plaza table, climbs up and takes the microphone — only then does your 50-second clock start. You play a card face down and declare what it is. That declaration can be a complete lie. If nobody challenges you, the effect happens anyway — invented or not.

But if someone slams the LIAR! button within the next few seconds, the two of you draw revolvers in the middle of the plaza:

  • You lied? You take the shot, lose a heart, and your real card is revealed to everyone.
  • You told the truth? The accuser goes down instead — and your effect still happens.

Everyone sees which of your two cards you spent, never what it was. The whole table can track your hand. That is entirely on purpose.

The night belongs to the impostor


When the sun sets, everyone acts at the same time, in secret — and now the card is real, no bluffing allowed. You visit houses, shield neighbors, watch doorways, poison whoever went out to do harm, swap someone's whole hand in the dark. Except whoever sleeps in the cell: they spend the night behind bars, doing nothing.

And the Bomber buries one more bomb. Nobody sees where. Not even the other impostors. If he is the only impostor at the table, he may even stay home — and swear in the morning that it was a quiet night.

Come morning the rooster crows, the doors swing open, everyone steps outside together — and that is when you find out whose garden already held two bombs. The house swells, shudders and vanishes in a cartoon mushroom cloud, roof cartwheeling all the way to the plaza.

The doors tell what the night did


In the morning, the report says which doors opened — never where to, never what for. Then every neighbor gives an alibi: "I stayed home", "I went to Ana's", "I went to the casino" — or would rather not say. Swore you stayed home and your door opened? The notebook puts a ⚠ next to your name for the whole table to see. Found the soil in your garden dug up? A bomb went in there — and only you know.

And the doormats talk too: every house that had a visitor wakes up with mud at the door — one pair of footprints per person who came. How many, never who. Three swear they went to Ana's and there are only two prints? The math is off, and the notebook marks the house with a ⚠. A print nobody owns up to? Somebody went out and isn't saying.

The impostor has an answer up their sleeve: Cover Up hides one door from the Doors of the Night — their own or an accomplice's. The door vanishes from the report. The mud they left on a doormat doesn't.

The street remembers


Everything the table sees ends up in the Neighbourhood Notebook: who played what and on which day, who got caught lying and which card flipped, who slept in the cell, which house went up — and since which night it had been mined, on a crooked little sign stuck in the rubble. Nobody has to memorise twelve neighbors: open the notebook and line the day up against the night. It never writes down a secret. Those are still yours, to tell… or to make up.

Call LIAR! and get it right, and you win more than the shot: you cross the street, lean on the fence and search the liar's garden. Bomb or no bomb — only you know. The whole street watched you look.

And when a house blows up, nobody pays a thing: the street shuffles out in its pajamas and walks to the round table for the Assembly. Everyone votes for someone or for SKIP — and only a neighbor with more votes than SKIP and than anyone else dies. Sometimes the table fires. Sometimes it just shrugs — and the impostor heard every word.

When talking stops working, call the meeting


Eight coins stop the day cold. Everyone puffs into a little cloud and reappears at the round table in the plaza, under a dramatic sunset. Almost two minutes of open-voice argument, a quick vote — and whoever the table condemns loses EVERY life to a cartoon firing squad.

Then their role is revealed. Good luck explaining yourself if you got it wrong.

And at the end, the paper tells all


When the match ends, an extra edition of The Neighbourhood News goes out to everybody, living or dead: who was who, what each neighbor declared and what they really held, day by day and night by night, and the headline of the match. That bluff nobody caught? It's in print. With your name on it.

Seven cards, day and night — and a lot more in Advanced


Every card does one thing by day and something completely different at night. The card you burn bluffing in daylight is the one you cannot use for real after dark. In Advanced each one also has a STREET trick — some you trigger, some fire by themselves — and card answers card: every day play but the Citizen's can be RESPONDED to by one specific card. Two triangles to draw in your head, not a table to memorise.

  • Vigilante — sentences someone to the plaza cell by day and walks them in at nightfall, in front of everybody; poisons whoever slipped out to do harm at night; and out on the pavement runs the ROUND: reads a house's bombs, how many and from which night. Answers the Thief.
  • Protector — grants immunity by day; makes a house bomb-proof at night; and simply by sitting in your hand it seals the block: peeks at you, or at any Citizen or Investor beside you, fail in silence. Answers the Reckless.
  • Reckless — by day it is hot potato: the card he just played goes to you and a random one of yours comes back; by night he swaps entire hands — the street only learns that somebody swapped; and every so often a peek slips out of him that even he never sees. Answers the Investigator.
  • Investor — invests this round's coin to collect four later; heads to the casino at night and bets big; and the floor of that bet is how far he walked the neighborhood that day. Answers the Vigilante.
  • Investigator — peeks at one card by day; stakes out a house at night and sees everyone who walked in; and if somebody goes through his hand, he gets their NAME. Answers the Protector.
  • Thief — steals coins by day; sabotages someone at night, and their next play goes off at random targets without a soul noticing; and on the street he has the QUICK EYE: one drawn card out of a neighbor's hand. Answers the Investor.
  • Citizen — rests like a good neighbor and earns a coin. At night he serves lemonade on the porch to his honest visitors — and counts how many crept into the yard to do harm, without knowing who. He answers nobody and nobody answers him. The perfect bait: accuse a real Citizen and you lose a heart for nothing.

Classic or Advanced


Classic is the whole game without the street and the responses: the cards with their day and night, the bluff, the search, the notebook, the assembly and the paper, and nothing else. It is the way in. After five finished matches, Advanced opens up: the Spy, the street tricks and the responses. The host picks in the lobby — and the whole table plays what the host picked.

Your room, your street


Create a room and choose who gets in: Steam friends (they join from an invite or their friends list) or Code only (listed nowhere — only whoever has the code walks in). Everyone else picks Join with a code or accepts the Steam invite. No Steam? The room is hosted on your PC, and anyone on the same network joins with your IP and the code. There are no strangers here: every table is people you brought.

The studio's community lives on Discord , one click away on the title screen and in the menu.

Neighbors who think


The bots do not cheat: each one decides only from what its own seat can see — just like you. They remember what you swore, accuse with a reason, vote on suspicion, bluff at the rate of their role and drop a line in the chat now and then. Any of them might be the impostor. Want bots at your table? In your room, +1 bot seats one more neighbor and the × sends one home. A room with just you and the bots is a whole match — and hosted on this PC, it does not even need the internet.

Voice over Steam, the way a street talks


At a Classic table, the voice belongs to everyone: by day every living neighbor hears every other, from any corner of the street. In Advanced, the day’s voice is proximity: full next to your robot, fading with distance — walking off in pairs is whispering — and whoever is at the table speaks into the microphone to the whole street. At the meeting and the assembly, everyone hears everyone. At night, silence — except on the impostors’ line: with two or more alive, they plot among themselves, by voice and chat, and the city hears nothing. Voice travels over Steam's network through the host, who hands each line only to those allowed to hear it — nobody receives anybody's address. Your mic starts open. A microphone icon on screen always shows whether you are being heard, and Options lets you switch to push-to-talk, test and calibrate your mic and set each neighbor’s volume.

There is something to do out there


Twelve toys scattered down the street — a playground, a trampoline, a fire hydrant, a fallen bicycle — and a neon-lit casino on the corner, with a roulette wheel, a one-armed bandit and dice out on the pavement.

What's in the box


  • 4 to 12 players online: rooms for Steam friends or by code, Steam overlay invites — and local network play without Steam.
  • Bots at your table: one +1 bot per seat; a room with just you and the bots is a whole match, no internet needed when this PC hosts it.
  • Two games: Classic to start with, and Advanced with the street and the responses — unlocked after 5 matches.
  • In-game voice over Steam: the whole table by day in Classic, proximity in Advanced, global at the meetings, muted at night — except the impostors’ line. Push-to-talk optional, a mic icon always in view and per-neighbor volume.
  • Text chat with a separate channel for the dead — who see everything and may tell no one — and an emote wheel.
  • The Neighbourhood Notebook during the match and The Neighbourhood News at the end.
  • Full controller support, from the menu to the victory, with an on-screen keyboard — and it plays on Steam Deck through Proton.
  • Accessibility: interface size, colorblind mode, steady camera and adjustable screen shake, per-channel volume, remappable keys and fast animations.
  • Streamer mode: on your screen, the other players become "Neighbor 1, 2…" and the room code stays hidden — the first switch in Options.
  • 12 colors and 12 accessories unlocked by playing. No in-game purchases, ever.
  • 15 achievements, some more embarrassing than others.
  • A guided tutorial that introduces the seven cards and both games and shows the key for every step, freezing the game while you learn — plus a short course of its own for Advanced. The illustrated manual is one key away.
  • Eight languages — English, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), French, German, Russian and Simplified Chinese — interface and subtitles, from day one.

One last thing


You will lie to your friends. They will lie to you. Somebody is going to blow up their own house by mistake — and the paper will put it on the front page.

That's the game.
